name: Jamal Costa

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government. Your answers stay confidential. What does a normal workday look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a small carpentry crew fitting timber stairs and dividing rooms on building sites. My vocational trade certificate gave me the basics, and the apprentices bring me the jobs where a drawing and the existing wall do not agree. I use AI every day to check a materials list and sort site photos, but I put the level on the actual stair before signing off. My partner Salma and I have two children at school, a mortgage, typical trade pay and about four months of expenses saved. A few other contractors work near us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew a faster photo list is fine if it keeps the stair measurements beside each picture. The app cannot feel a loose stair tread under a work boot.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My fitting hours should continue in this mild world, and four months saved gives us some room. I would still make the apprentices measure twice, because a wrong cut costs materials and paid time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading stair jobs and using the AI photo sorter I already know. In the first year I would add the tread height and level reading to each handover before the next crew arrives.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about income. I am more bothered by a missing dimension than a software change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which photo needs a measurement beside it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The top tread often meets a floor that is not quite level. I would mark its height in the photo caption before anyone cuts the trim.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy a different app?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. The company tool works well enough, and Salma and I would rather keep cash for family costs than pay for another subscription.

say: **Photo lists** help only when stair dimensions remain beside each image for the next site crew.
**Physical checks** still reveal a loose tread.
think: My **stair-fitting hours** look safe in this mild plateau because hands-on work continues on site.
Four months saved gives **household room** for ordinary surprises.
do: **Keep** leading stairs and using the current photo tool.
**Add** tread heights and level readings to each handover.
feel: **Calm** about income, alert to missing dimensions.
S0.quote: The app cannot feel a loose stair tread under a work boot.
fieldNote: He already uses **AI daily** for photos and materials, with physical checks at the stair.
His **four-month cushion** makes this minor software change financially manageable while mortgage payments continue.

steps.text: Keep stair-fitting jobs and current AI photo sorting

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the buying office and schedules change before robots can fit stairs on site. I want a new delivery planner tested against the narrow houses where our timber orders usually go wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A good plan might save trips, but a wrong kit can waste my crew’s paid day. With a mortgage and only four months saved, repeated short weeks would bite even though some contractors nearby could hire me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would test the planner on six stair jobs, logging deliveries, rework and actual hours. During the first year I would bring the results to the site manager and keep the old checking process on any job type the planner misses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about lost paid hours, but curious about better ordering. I want numbers from site, not an office slide.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which job type would expose an error?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A stair in an older house may need a narrower tread at the top. I would compare the delivered piece with the opening and mark the delay if it needs replacing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell your crew if the planner works?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say we can use it for that kind of stair, then still check each delivery. A success on six stair jobs is a start, not permission to stop measuring.

say: **Buying and schedules** change before capable robots can fit physical stairs on building sites.
think: Wrong **stair kits** could waste full paid crew days when the delivered timber does not match an older opening.
Our **four-month reserve** cannot cover repeated short weeks.
do: **Test** the planner on six stair jobs with delivery and rework records.
**Keep** manual checks on job types the planner misses.
feel: **Anxious** about pay, interested in evidence from site.
S1.quote: A success on six stair jobs is a start, not permission to stop measuring.
fieldNote: He tests **new planning AI** through delivery, rework and paid hours.
His **income risk** comes from repeated wrong kits and unpaid hours, despite some nearby contractors offering work.

steps.text: Learn delivery planner on six stair jobs with actual records
Keep manual stair checks on job types planner misses

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my crew that thinking AI can handle buying and drawings by 2028, while capable building robots arrive around 2031. We still have hands-on stair work during the three-year gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a robot can fit stairs properly, our crew may lose paid days after 2031. Four months saved will not protect our mortgage for a long search, and some nearby jobs may carry lower pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for paid robot-layout practice on an empty test room and learn the stop control before any live site use. If the contractor funds a site-measurement course for a posted local checking vacancy, I would complete it; after 2028 I would apply for that role only if its wage covers mortgage and school costs and the robot work passes a real safety trial.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, but I would rather test a machine than argue from a distance. I need a posted site-checking role to pay our mortgage, not just sound interesting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the safety trial real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would have the robot measure a stair with a crooked wall and stop it if the tread height is wrong. The crew should record both the failed and successful attempts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would Salma support the move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Salma would ask about the wage and school pickup hours. I think she would back a posted local job if those numbers worked, but I would not decide for her.

say: **2028 thinking AI** changes buying before capable site robots can fit stairs around 2031.
think: Robots may cut **paid crew days** after 2031.
Four months saved and **some nearby jobs** may not replace the same wage.
do: **Learn** robot layout and stop controls in a paid safe-room trial.
**Complete** funded measuring course for posted local checking vacancy.
**Apply** after 2028 only with bill-covering wage and proven robot safety.
feel: **Anxious** about job days, willing to test tools.
S2.quote: I need a posted site-checking role to pay our mortgage, not just sound interesting.
fieldNote: He links **paid robot practice** to safe controls before live use.
His **application** needs funded training, a posted local role, bill-covering wages and a real safety trial.

steps.text: Learn robot layout and stop controls in paid empty-room trial
Complete funded measurement course for posted local checking vacancy
Apply after 2028 for posted local checking only with bill-covering pay and proven robot safety

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years lets me see more than a demonstration before thinking AI reaches the office in 2031. Capable field robots follow around 2034, and a trial should include old stairs as well as new ones.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My children will be older, but the mortgage may still be there. I could move into site quality work if the employer pays to train me and a real local opening covers our bills; a certificate alone would not feed the family.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take employer-paid quality training on an actual site if a posted local vacancy at bill-covering pay is offered. In the first year after 2031 I would apply for that job after completing training and checking its safety duties; otherwise I would keep leading the stair crew.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Still anxious about the wage, though five years gives time to inspect a role properly. I would rather know the daily work than guess from a title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What safety duty would you check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A site quality job should let me reject a robot-fitted stair before a family uses it. The employer should write that authority into the role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If the posted job pays less than your current one?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could accept a modest drop if the wage still covers the mortgage, school and food without using savings every month. Salma and I would compare the offer together.

say: **Old-stair trials** should precede capable robots that can fit physical stairs around 2034.
**Quality staff** need authority to reject unsafe robot work.
think: A **quality role** could fit if paid training and real work exist.
The **mortgage and children** still require bill-covering pay.
do: **Take** employer-paid quality training for posted local bill-covering vacancy.
**Apply** after 2031 if trained and role permits rejecting unsafe treads.
feel: **Anxious** about wages, with time to inspect real duties.
S3.quote: A site quality job should let me reject a robot-fitted stair before a family uses it.
fieldNote: He makes **rejection authority** a condition of the quality move.
His **training and application** depend on employer payment, a posted local vacancy, bill-covering wages and written safety duties.

steps.text: Take employer-paid quality training for posted local bill-covering vacancy
Apply after 2031 for posted local bill-covering quality role if trained and safety authority written
Keep leading stair crew if no suitable post opens

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade puts thinking AI in 2036 and capable building robots around 2039. I would use the time to make the mortgage smaller and teach apprentices to question a perfect drawing when a wall is crooked.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be in my fifties when capable robots reach the site. Ten years gives time to build an extra buffer, but I still need paid work beyond that; the children may be leaving school and making their own choices.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the stair crew job and pay an extra forty toward the mortgage from each full pay cheque if household bills are covered. In the first year after 2036 I would apply for a posted local site-quality role only if its wage covers our bills, training is paid and the role lets me reject unsafe robot work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about later work, but not rushed. I could make a small payment every full week and still keep the family reserve intact.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if you have a short pay week?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would skip the extra forty and pay the ordinary bills first. The four-month reserve is for pay gaps, not for pretending an extra mortgage payment is regular.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach an apprentice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would make the apprentice mark a wall with a level before looking at the generated drawing. The site can be wrong too, so I would check the mark twice.

say: **2036 thinking AI** arrives before capable building robots can fit stairs around 2039.
**Apprentices** should compare drawings with real walls.
think: The **long runway** allows extra mortgage payments from full site wages if regular family bills remain covered.
I still need **paid work** after robots arrive.
do: **Keep** leading the stair crew on site.
**Pay** forty extra on mortgage from full cheques only after bills.
**Apply** after 2036 for posted local quality only with bill-covering pay, paid training and safety authority.
feel: **Uneasy** about later wages, with time to reduce debt.
S4.quote: The four-month reserve is for pay gaps, not for pretending an extra mortgage payment is regular.
fieldNote: He separates **new debt payment** from existing savings.
His **later application** keeps wage, paid training and safety authority as conditions for accepting a posted local role.

steps.text: Keep leading stair crew on current sites
Pay forty extra on mortgage from full cheques after bills
Apply after 2036 for posted local quality with bill-covering pay, paid training and safety authority

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most, because stair-fitting robots around 2031 could take paid crew days while the mortgage and school costs remain. Paid training for a posted local quality role with authority to reject unsafe work would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who gets to say the robot fitted a stair badly. I want the person who checks a robot-fitted tread to have a wage and the right to send it back.

portrait: **Jamal Costa**, 43, leads a stair carpentry crew and holds a vocational trade certificate.
He and partner Salma have **two school-age children**, a mortgage, typical pay and about four months of expenses saved.
He uses **AI daily** for photos and materials, and would learn robot controls in a paid safe-room trial.
In **AGI by 2031**, he seeks a real local quality role with paid training and rejection authority.
The **2028 picture** worries him because robots could cut crew days before the family has a bigger buffer.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could reduce paid stair-fitting days after 2031 while mortgage and school bills continue.
whatWouldHelp: Employer-paid **quality training** linked to a posted local bill-covering role would give him another income path.
Written **rejection authority** would let him stop unsafe robot-fitted stairs.
headlineQuote: I want the person who checks a robot-fitted tread to have a wage and the right to send it back.
